steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Atomic model: A representation of the structure of an atom. Our understanding of the atom has changed over time as new evidence was discovered. | Nucleus: The tiny, dense centre of an atom containing protons and neutrons. It has a positive charge due to the protons. | Electron shell: A fixed energy level at a set distance from the nucleus in which electrons orbit the nucleus. | Isotope: Atoms of the same element that have the same number of protons but a different number of neutrons. They have the same atomic number but different mass numbers.

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Foundation Describe the plum pudding model and explain how the alpha scattering experiment disproved it. | Foundation A boron atom has atomic number 5 and mass number 11. Calculate the number of protons, neutrons and electrons. | Foundation Write the electron configuration for: (a) nitrogen (atomic number 7), (b) magnesium (atomic number 12), (c) potassium (atomic number 19).
